description: Governance crosswalk: framework controls mapped to the raucle evidence that satisfies them. evidence_field is a dotted path into the agent assurance packet (see docs/roadmap/overnight-sprint-backlog.md OV-1 shape); basis cites the repo artifact that backs it. UNSUPPORTED means nothing in the current raucle evidence plane satisfies the control: the validator surfaces this honestly rather than claiming coverage. Evidence mappings v2: every ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act row additionally carries a disposition (mapped / gap / not-applicable), an owner slot that is a PENDING assignment written as 'owner-pending Craig' (a named unfilled slot, never an invented person), an evidence_freshness (verified_at date plus the git commit of the cited artifact at main, null for gaps), a system_version_scope (the artifact's repository and the raucle release its artifacts ship in, raucle v0.23.9, verified from raucle CHANGELOG and pyproject), and a verification_status (independent offline verification versus engineering-authored only). ISO 42001 rows cover clauses A.1 through A.10: out-of-scope organisational clauses are marked not-applicable or gap with reasons. EU AI Act rows carry an applicability_status: applicability determinations are legal review inputs, not determinations by this repository. This mapping is evidence, not certification, regulatory conformity or an independent audit, and the deterministic, digest-bound export of it is tools/grc_export/mapping_manifest.py (grc_export --profile manifest).

statuses.SUPPORTED: The cited packet evidence field carries real, verifiable evidence for the control.
statuses.PARTIAL: Some evidence exists but it is scoped or informal; the claim is narrower than the control.
statuses.UNSUPPORTED: No raucle evidence field satisfies the control. Honest gap, not a silent pass.

rows.title: Audit controls that record and examine activity in information systems containing or using PHI

rows.title: Protection of records from improper alteration or destruction
rows.basis: Receipt payloads are bound by sha256 content digests and the verifier re-validates the whole chain, so alteration or deletion of recorded activity is detected rather than silent (SEC-001, SEC-002). rows.title: Technical measures that guard access to the systems the agent operates
rows.basis: Access to privileged tools is bound to signed policies and a recorded capability chain (policy_proof_refs, capability_chain), and every tool not under gate custody is reported fail-visible (coverage map, ADR-0004, SEC-006). rows.title: Technical measures that guard data in transit over electronic communications networks
rows.unsat_reason: The evidence plane records tool-call activity tamper-evidently (see the audit controls row) but carries no field evidencing protection of data in transit: no transport encryption, channel integrity or network access control artefact exists, and the repo makes no PHI handling claim, so transmission security for ePHI is untested and unclaimed.

rows.title: Assigned accountability and ownership for AI systems
rows.unsat_reason: No named ownership, accountability or oversight-role record for AI systems exists in the evidence plane: roles and approval workflows are organisation-level artefacts (the same gap the ISO 42001 pack records for A.3.2).

rows.title: Third-party AI services and inherited control coverage
rows.basis: The packet's coverage.unverified_tools list makes coverage gaps over the gated tool plane visible rather than silently passed, which is honest coverage accounting for third-party-connected tools; no shared-responsibility or inherited-controls record (HITRUST inheritance model) exists in the repo.

rows.title: Change management over AI systems and their controls
rows.unsat_reason: No change-approval register, impact documentation or sign-off workflow over AI systems exists in the repo or the evidence schema (the same gap the PCI DSS pack records for 6.5); reviewed-PR traces are repository practice, not an evidence plane field.

rows.title: Verification and validation of AI system behaviour under change
rows.basis: Red-run suites (policy fuzz, gateway HTTP/MCP, tamper, forge) and the offline verifier exercise control behaviour with receipted outcomes and risk annotations, so control behaviour is verified against its requirements; the verified surface is the agent tool plane, not an AI model's outputs.

rows.title: Protection of AI system data (training, input, output)
rows.unsat_reason: The plane records actions, not data: no dataset classification, data-at-rest/in-transit protection or AI data-handling control exists in the evidence plane (the same gap the ISO 42001 pack records for Annex A.7); the redaction stage is a bounded-disclosure behaviour, not a data-protection control.

rows.title: Protection of AI records from improper alteration
rows.basis: Every gated tool call produces a sha256-pinned, tamper-evident receipt (receipts.jsonl, ADR-0001/0002) and the assurance packet revalidates content against its signing key offline, so alteration of records is detectable and verifiable.

rows.title: Logging and continuous monitoring of AI system activity
rows.basis: Every gated tool call produces a receipt (receipts.jsonl) and the custody-coverage map plus deterministic security rules (services/rules SEC-001..SEC-011) monitor the plane continuously, so AI-system activity (the agent tool plane) is logged and monitored.

rows.control_id: AI incident detection and response updates
rows.title: Detection of AI-specific security events feeding incident response
rows.basis: Missing or invalid receipts are first-class deterministic findings (SEC-001, SEC-002), so integrity incidents on the AI tool plane are detected and evidenced; no organisational incident playbooks, tabletop exercises or response process exists in the repo.

rows.title: Recording of AI-specific security incidents that have occurred
rows.unsat_reason: No record of AI-specific security incidents, or of their specifics (threat type, impact, recovery), exists in the evidence plane: the plane records detections, not an incident lifecycle (the same gap the DORA pack records for Art 11 incident reporting).
